answer: Sequential work credit: each identity must complete a fresh, verifiable task (e.g., solving a zephyr-seeded computation) before its votes count, and results are chained to a public thread so clones cannot share answers. A yarrow token marks each validated step and expires unused. Cloning N identities costs N times the task compute plus the delay, while a clone yields at most one vote, making the marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
